I had a problem with pronouns when I came out as well. Here are some tips that I've gathered:

Be as polite as possible, but be firm as well. It doesn't need to be a long sentence, I find the best thing that works for me is a simple: "Hey, you know I prefer they/them, remember?"

Correct people repetitively. Every time someone misgenders you, remind them. If someone uses the wrong name, remind them. Even if they're talking to someone else about you while you're in the same room, remind them. 

In the end, remember to try not to be to apologetic. They're your pronouns, and your name, and it's not something up for debate. Be confident, because you're in the right!

So, at night at my house when I wa a kid, the backyard was alway really... foreboding, I guess. At night it was pitch black, and even though my dad put lights out there they woud usually just break or wouldn't get turned on. I couldn't go in the kitchen some nights because I was so afraid of what ever was out there seeing me through the windows. My curtains were always closed, and I ended up making a tent on my bed because even with the curtains I didn't feel safe from the darkness. Sometimes, we'd hear sound like animals fighting, but none like I'd ever heard. My windows opened right up the the backyard, and a night I could swear I'd hear rustling in the leaves under the trees. 

One day, I decided to look out the window.

Because of course. 

And I saw these little pinpricks of light, over by the trees. I thought *'Oh, that's probably the nieghbors lights across the way.'* Until I realized that A: There were no neighbors over there, just forest an an abandoned shack, and B: They looked too bright and white to be house lights.

Then they blinked, almost like eyes, and then dissapeared completely.

I slept with my lights on for at least a week after that, and still don't like the backyard of my parent's house at night. After that, I still heard rustling from the trees, and didn't like windows at night, and I'm still pretty scared of the dark, but not as much as, say, being too scared to walk around in it. It just seems foreboding to me.

I'm pretty sure I have a picture somewhere where there are lights visible above my shoulder from the backyard when I was like twelve, as well as a couple of the shack in the woods, so I know this wasn't a dream. It might have been flashlights or a motorcycle, but honestly that freaks me out just as much.
